title: Measuring the Marginal Value of Sandboxed Emulation for Validator‑Assisted LLM NetOps Artifacts
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) comparing a deterministic validator alone versus the same validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation on synthetic intent→configuration tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using the declared/requested model "gpt-5-mini" (provider: openai_responses) we ran Npairs = 720 complete paired episodes. The deterministic validator flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + emulation, with at most one repair-stage call allowed) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows total model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared-initial + 1 repair-stage). These outcomes lie far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, artifact-grounded quantitative results, a concise explanation of provider-call audit fields, an artifact-identified discordant episode (pair-000504), and evidence-grounded discussion of boundary conditions where guarded stages are likely to matter. Related literature on agentic NetOps, emulation-based validation, and mature configuration analyzers is cited to position the findings [1]–[3].

sections.introduction:
Generative language models are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations and NetOps workflows. Operational deployment demands that generated artifacts satisfy syntactic correctness, workflow-order constraints, and higher-order safety/policy invariants. A common industrial and research mitigation is a generate→validate→(repair)→execute workflow, sometimes augmented by post-validation sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures that static validators miss. Prior surveys and system reports argue for workflow-centred evaluation and layered mitigation but provide limited large-scale, preregistered, paired measures of the marginal value added by emulation when a strong static validator is already in place [1]–[3].

Research question and contributions. We preregistered a paired confirmatory study to answer: under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Our contributions are: (1) a machine-readable preregistered paired design and faithful autonomous execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with full run accounting; (3) an explicit, artifact-anchored clarification of provider-call audit fields and the one discordant episode identification; and (4) a concise operational interpretation and boundary conditions for the negligible marginal effect observed.
sections.related_work:
Workflow-centred mitigations and verification tools. Surveys and architectural reports emphasize that reliability of agentic NetOps depends chiefly on the surrounding validator, tool orchestration, and execution safeguards rather than the model alone; they recommend workflow-centred evaluation that includes sandboxed replay and rollback-aware scoring [1].

Emulation and verifier precedents. Research prototypes pair generation with determinisitic verifiers (e.g., Batfish-style configuration analysis) and with emulation to exercise temporal and stateful behaviors that static rules may not capture; reported gains are heterogeneous and task-dependent [2]. Multimodal co-pilot systems and recent agentic NetOps architectures illustrate both promise and the need for careful V&V pipelines when topology and stepwise state changes matter [3]. These prior works motivated a paired design that reuses the same sampled candidate for both conditions (shared_initial_candidate) so that any between-condition differences must arise solely from downstream guarded-stage processing (emulation observation or repair).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and paired design. We preregistered study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e with a paired-binary confirmatory estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Planned Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440) and a minimum effect-of-interest = 0.20 for power planning. Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance after deterministic reseed up to two times; irrecoverable parser failures would be handled deterministically per the missingness plan. The preregistration fixed the analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1), the primary exact McNemar test, and a paired-bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729).

Task bank, topology templates, and validator. Confirmatory items were produced deterministically from an intent_configuration_repair_v1 generator covering three abstract vendor‑CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Each task manifest includes explicit intent, initial_state, expected_final_state, required_command_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies. The baseline validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) applies deterministic, rule-based checks: vendor parsing, command canonicalization, order/sequence constraints (e.g., make-before-break), group-level activity constraints, protected-interface invariants, and final-state conformance. The validator emits a binary detection flag and a validator_trace object with detailed parsed counts and violation codes.

Guarded pipeline and emulation harness. The guarded condition runs the same validator and then executes the candidate in a sandboxed emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology and executes normalized CLI commands against vendor-abstracted virtual devices. Emulation records runtime observations (interface transitions, transient concurrent states, MTU/VLAN application effects, and topology-level reachability) and maps those observations to runtime-observation rules that can trigger an additional guarded detection not expressible as the validator’s static rules. The emulation mapping is conservative by design—intended to surface runtime-only violations rather than overflag benign transient states.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and repair policy. For each pair the pipeline performed exactly one initial model generation (shared across both conditions). The preregistered repair policy permitted at most one repair-stage model invocation per task, executed only after initial generation and downstream observations for the guarded condition. This design isolates guarded-stage contributions to either emulation-derived observations or to permitted repair activity. The declared/requested model recorded in the run configuration is "gpt-5-mini" (provider: openai_responses); the archived model configuration records that no explicit temperature value was supplied by the client (recorded as null).

Provider-call audit fields: concise clarification. The archived deterministic reconciliation and execution manifest provide audited model-call counts and stage-level breakdowns. Key audited facts from the archived execution are: total model_calls_used = 721; stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 720, repair: 1}; and provider-stage condition_counts reported the provider-side call mapping as {shared: 720, guarded: 1}. These audited fields mean: 720 shared-initial generation calls (one per paired task) plus one additional repair-stage model call performed during guarded processing for a single episode. The provider-side condition_counts map model-call events to pipeline stages (not to episode totals) and thus should not be conflated with episode accounting—episode accounting is independently reported as completed_episode_count = 1440 and complete_pair_count = 720 in the deterministic reconciliation artifact. The analysis and Results use the episode-level accounting (720 complete pairs) and the provider-call audit to explain how many model calls and repair invocations occurred during the run.

Analysis procedures. The primary confirmatory analysis used the pre-registered paired-binary executor aligned with an exact McNemar two-sided test and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729). Secondary per-class and per-vendor analyses were pre-specified as exploratory with Bonferroni-adjusted CIs; no irrecoverable technical exclusions occurred, so the primary analysis used complete-pair handling with no pair removed for technical failure.
sections.results:
Primary aggregated outcomes (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 720. Contingency counts: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. These numeric outputs are taken verbatim from the archived analysis artifacts.

Discordant-pair attribution and repair accounting (artifact-identified). Provider-call auditing and the terminal factual accounting identify the unique discordant pair as pair-000504. The archived raw-results record for pair-000504 shows: baseline episode (task-000504-baseline) had score = 0 and model_calls_used = 1; guarded episode (task-000504-guarded) had score = 1 and model_calls_used = 2, indicating that a repair-stage invocation occurred in the guarded processing for that episode. Across the entire confirmatory run the audited stage_counts are shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1, and total model_calls_used = 721. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the permitted sources of between-condition discordance are (i) a guarded-emulation runtime observation not codified as a validator violation, or (ii) the single repair-stage invocation linked to pair-000504. The archived per-episode artifacts contain the validator_trace and repair trace for pair-000504 for independent inspection.

Representative diagnostics. Representative per-episode scoring traces (several examples archived) show validator_trace fields with parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation_count; the majority of shared_initial candidates in the confirmatory set produced violation_count = 0 under the validator, consistent with the baseline success rate of 719/720. Difficulty stratification from the terminal factual accounting reports: extreme: 90 (12.5%), hard: 180 (25.0%), medium: 90 (12.5%), very_hard: 360 (50.0%).
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded-stage aggregate benefit negligible? The archived evidence supports three artifact-grounded explanations.

1) Validator ceiling effect and task-rule alignment. The baseline validator encoded the workflow checks exercised by the curated tasks (patterns such as shutdown_configure_restore, make_before_break_uplink_switchover, paired_link_atomic_mtu_change). The high baseline success rate (719/720) indicates that validator coverage closely matched the task bank, leaving little headroom for emulation to add detection coverage.

2) Curated inclusion and reduced adversarial exposure. The confirmatory tasks were deterministically generated and required vendor-parser acceptance for inclusion; this restricted the confirmatory set to parser-validated, policy-constrained scenarios. Such curation reduces the prevalence of runtime-only faults that emulation would uniquely reveal.

3) Shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity. The design reused the same sampled initial candidate for both conditions and permitted at most one repair invocation per task; the provider audit shows exactly one recorded repair across the run. Thus the single discordant episode corresponds to that single repair or a guarded-emulation-only observation; the archived per-episode traces permit auditors to resolve which occurred for pair-000504.

Operational implications. For operator environments with a high-coverage static validator aligned to expected intents and with upstream parser-based prevalidation, an automated sandboxed-emulation stage may provide negligible marginal detection benefit at scale. This does not generalize to adversarial, uncurated, or production-like distributions where emulation can surface runtime semantics and side-effects that static rule sets miss. Pragmatically: (a) invest in richer validators when throughput and low-latency are priorities; (b) reserve guarded emulation for high-risk or high-impact changes; (c) use adversarial/fuzz banks to identify validator gaps. The archived artifacts provide concrete seed cases to guide such extensions.
sections.conclusion:
We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator against the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration task bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Provider-call auditing shows total model_calls_used = 721 with a single recorded repair-stage invocation corresponding to the unique guarded-only detection (pair-000504). We interpret the near-zero effect as arising from validator ceiling effects and the curated, parser-validated task design. Follow-up work should target adversarial and production-like task banks, expanded vendor-CLI diversity, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages add substantive operational value.

Reproducibility pointers. The canonical archived execution bundle (referenced in the execution manifest) contains the per-episode raw results, validator traces, deterministic_reconciliation (episode accounting and provider-call audit), and the analysis artifacts used to produce the numeric outputs reported above. Independent auditors can locate the discordant episode (pair-000504) and inspect its validator_trace and repair trace in the archived raw results for forensic mapping of the guarded-only detection to the recorded repair call. For brevity we do not reproduce per-file checksums in-text; the execution manifest and archived bundle are the canonical provenance sources for those details.

Declared/requested language model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses). Deterministic validator used: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration id: f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest). Execution accounting (archived): completed_episode_count = 1440, complete_pair_count = 720, model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared-initial + 1 repair-stage). Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the NetOps topic family and constrained the pre-lock master prompt; after the autonomy lock the agentic pipeline autonomously performed literature selection, preregistration, code/prompt generation, experiment execution, analysis, autonomous peer-review and manuscript drafting. No manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock. The execution manifest and archived bundle named in the preregistration serve as the canonical reproducibility bundle for per-file provenance.
limitations: Synthetic, deterministically generated task bank and parser-based inclusion create limited ecological diversity and a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and a single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across other models and validator families.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally remove between-condition generation variability; this design isolates guarded-stage contributions but excludes potential benefits from independent re-generation in the guarded arm.
Emulation fidelity is limited by the sandbox harness used; higher-fidelity vendor-specific control-plane models or longer-lived state interactions could change outcomes in other regimes.

The study was powered for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this preregistered regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation and provider-call auditing; these are documented in the archived reconciliation and manifest artifacts.
